payload.title: Add a user-only correcting entry for task state
payload.description: Add a user-only command that appends a correcting ledger event setting a task's status directly, with a required reason, so a wrong state is fixed without replaying lifecycle transitions that never happened.
payload.context: The ledger is append-only, and the only way to correct a task's state today is to replay ordinary transitions through their gates. When a gate was skipped on the way in, that can deadlock: a landed todo task with unapproved plan items could only get back to assumed by going through revisit, submitted, ready and underway and reconciling again, and those transitions now sit in its history as if they described real events. Accounting solves the same problem with a correcting journal entry: never erase, post a new entry that says what it corrects and why. The command should record a distinct correction event carrying the before and after status, the reason and the actor; refuse to run from an agent, as approve does; skip lifecycle gates but keep data invariants (no unknown status, no duplicate or foreign IDs); and show in task history as a correction. Repairing drift between the database and the ledger is a separate concern.

payload.title: Decide moving Endless's records off the default branch
payload.description: Decide moving the records Endless commits by itself (ledger entries, task-field and decision mirrors, lessons, verify reports) from a project's default branch to a separate branch, linked to main by a commit trailer
payload.plan:
## Open questions

**Q1. What is the trailer's key?**

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| A. Fixed: `endless-main: <sha>` | One key to search for in every repo. | Reads wrong in a repo whose default branch is not main. |
| B. Named for the default branch: `endless-<primary_branch>: <sha>` | Says which branch the SHA is on. | The key differs per repo, so a reader must know the branch name to search; renaming the branch changes the key for new commits only. |
| C. Fixed key, branch in the value: `endless-base: main@<sha>` (or two trailers, `endless-branch` and `endless-commit`) | One key everywhere, and it still names the branch. | none |

Recommendation: C.

**Q2. What is the branch called?**

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| A. `endless-meta` | Matches the separate-repo naming convention. | none |
| B. `endless/meta` (a namespace) | Leaves room for other Endless branches under `endless/`. | A branch named `endless` can then never exist, since git cannot hold both. |

Recommendation: A.

**Q3. How does Endless write to the branch while main is checked out?**

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| A. Git's low-level commands (`hash-object`, `mktree`, `commit-tree`, `update-ref`) with no checkout | No extra directory; no working tree to get dirty. | Reading a record means `git show` against the branch instead of opening a file. |
| B. A dedicated worktree of the branch (e.g. under `.endless/worktrees/`) | Records stay ordinary files that tools and people can open. | One more working tree that can be left dirty or deleted by hand. |

Recommendation: A for writes, with reads going through Endless's commands.

**Q4. When does a clone fetch the branch?**

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| A. Before every read of records | Always current. | A network call on each read; offline reads need a fallback to the local copy. |
| B. On a schedule, alongside main-sync's fetch | Reads stay local and fast. | Records can be minutes stale. |

Recommendation: B, with A available as an explicit refresh.

**Q5. What happens to records already on main?**

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| A. Copy them to the new branch, then delete them from main's tree in one commit | Main's tree is clean from then on; history keeps the old copies. | One large deletion commit on main. |
| B. Leave existing records on main; only new records go to the branch | No large commit. | Records split across two places forever. |

Recommendation: A.
payload.context:
Endless commits to a project's default branch far more often than at lands: ledger entries, task-field and decision mirrors, lessons and verify reports, each as its own commit. They clutter main's history, and GitHub names a push-triggered CI run after the push's newest commit, so runs get titled "Endless: record ledger entry" or "lesson: ..." (seen on go-dt). Mike, 2026-10-29: he wants a way to keep these commits from cluttering history, and had not considered writing them to another branch.

Settled with Mike, 2026-10-29 (in E-2375's session):
- Not all of .endless/ moves. Files that change with code stay on main and task branches: config.json, each task's verify.toml and suite files, and the suite rules (tasks/CLAUDE.md, shared harness files). Records Endless writes by itself move: ledger entries, task-field and decision mirrors, LESSONS.md, verify reports.
- Records link to main's commits through a commit-message trailer, lowercase, not through tags (one tag per main commit would flood the tag list release tooling reads). Ledger entries already name landed SHAs and verify reports carry the SHA they tested.
- A separate repo for the records (convention <repo>-endless or <repo>-endless-meta) is a later configuration option on the same design: only the remote holding the branch differs.
- README.md links prominently to the records branch. Main's tree no longer showing task records is counted as a plus: some people would see them as bloat in the repo they work in.
- Pushes to the records branch start no CI run under workflows that trigger only on main and dev, as gomion's generated ones do.

payload.title: Refuse to verify a task that has already landed
payload.description: Refuse `endless task verify` on an already-landed task with a message saying it landed (and where), instead of the reconciliation gate's false 'the code changed' error
payload.context:
Running `endless task verify E-2419` after E-2419 landed (status `assumed`, branch HEAD a1cfd49 on main) refused with:

    Error: E-2419 cannot be verified yet:
      - the code changed since the last reconciliation; reconcile again

The message is false. The reconciliation gate (internal/reconcilegate, `Fingerprint`) fingerprints the branch as the patch-id of its diff from the merge-base with main to HEAD. Once the branch is in main, the merge-base is HEAD, the diff is empty, and the fingerprint is "empty" — which never matches the one stored at reconciliation. So every landed task gets this error, and reconciling again cannot clear it.

Verifying a landed task should not run at all: a suite is a land-time gate (.endless/tasks/CLAUDE.md), and a pass would call `unlanded.record_pass` (src/endless/verify_cmd.py), moving the task's state on a run that means nothing.

## Open questions

**Q1. What is the trailer's key?** The value names Git's default branch and the commit, e.g. `main@<sha>`. A trailer key must be letters, digits and hyphens: `git interpret-trailers --parse` ignores a line whose key has other characters.

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| A. `endless-default: main@<sha>` | Names Endless. | Reads as a default of Endless's, which it is not. |
| B. `git-default: main@<sha>` | Uses Git's own term. | Does not say Endless wrote it, so it could collide with another tool's trailer. |
| C. `Endless[git-default]: main@<sha>` | Names Endless and gives a pattern for later annotations. | Git does not recognize it as a trailer, so `git interpret-trailers` and `git log --format=%(trailers)` never see it. |
| D. `endless-git-default: main@<sha>` | Names Endless and uses Git's term; the `endless-<name>` prefix is a pattern for later annotations, and git recognizes it. | none |
| E. `endless-base: main@<sha>` | Names Endless; short. | "base" is not Git's term for the default branch. |

fields.description: Update a project's .endless/tasks/CLAUDE.md to the rules this Endless ships when `endless project init` is re-run, unless someone has edited that project's copy.
fields.plan:
# Update an unedited .endless/tasks/CLAUDE.md on project init

Handed over from E-2349 (Mike asked its session to send it). Filed from E-2257
on Mike's go-ahead, 2026-10-22.

## Problem

Every project Endless manages gets a rules file at `.endless/tasks/CLAUDE.md`.
It tells an agent how a task's own folder works and how to write a verify
suite. Endless writes it the first time `endless project init` runs, and never
touches it again.

Re-running `endless project init` is meant to bring a project up to date
(E-2349's EQ-82). For this file it doesn't. So when Endless changes the rules,
as E-2419 did, every existing project keeps the old ones: go-cfgstore and
homelab still teach the old suite form today.

## Behaviour

Re-running init updates the file to the rules this Endless ships, but only if
nobody has edited the project's copy:

- If the file is exactly what init last wrote into this project, replace it.
- If init has no record for this project (the copy predates this feature), and
  the file is exactly some version Endless has shipped, replace it.
- Otherwise leave it alone, and say it was edited locally and not updated.

"Exactly" is judged by a hash of the file's contents, so Endless never has to
keep the old text itself.

## Where the records live

- **What init wrote into a project** belongs to that project, so it is
  recorded in the project's own history (the ledger) and travels with a clone.
- **Which versions Endless has shipped** belongs to Endless itself, so each
  install knows them with no download or setup.
- If both are kept in one place, it can hold other kinds of shipped file later,
  not just this one (Mike).
- Hashing and storage are done in Go; everything is moving there (Mike).

## Content

- A list of what changed may go in the file itself, as text a reader sees
  (Mike).

## In the endless repo itself

- Running init from a task's worktree records into that worktree's sandbox,
  not the main database.

## Blocked by

- E-2419, which changed the rules text. It has landed.

## Open questions

**Q1. What is the trailer's key?** The value names Git's default branch and the commit, e.g. `main@<sha>`. A trailer key must be letters, digits and hyphens: `git interpret-trailers --parse` ignores a line whose key has other characters.

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| A. `endless-default: main@<sha>` | Names Endless. | Reads as a default of Endless's, which it is not. |
| B. `git-default: main@<sha>` | Uses Git's own term. | Does not say Endless wrote it, so it could collide with another tool's trailer. |
| C. `Endless[git-default]: main@<sha>` | Names Endless and gives a pattern for later annotations. | Git does not recognize it as a trailer, so `git interpret-trailers` and `git log --format=%(trailers)` never see it. |
| D. `endless-git-default: main@<sha>` | Names Endless and uses Git's term; the `endless-<name>` prefix is a pattern for later annotations, and git recognizes it. | none |
| E. `endless-base: main@<sha>` | Names Endless; short. | "base" is not Git's term for the default branch. |
| F. `endless_git-default: main@<sha>` | Names Endless; underscore separates the namespace. | Git does not recognize it: an underscore is not allowed in a trailer key. |
| G. `endless:git-default: main@<sha>` | Names Endless; colon reads as a namespace. | Git splits at the first colon, so it parses as key `endless` with value `git-default: main@<sha>`. |

Recommendation: D. (Options A to C, F and G were Mike's, 2026-10-29; F and G tested with git interpret-trailers --parse.)

**Q2. What is the branch called?**

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| A. `endless-meta` | Matches the separate-repo naming convention. | none |
| B. `endless/meta` (a namespace) | Leaves room for other Endless branches under `endless/`. | A branch named `endless` can then never exist, since git cannot hold both. |

Recommendation: A.

**Q3. How does Endless write to the branch while main is checked out?**

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| A. Git's low-level commands (`hash-object`, `mktree`, `commit-tree`, `update-ref`) with no checkout | No extra directory; no working tree to get dirty. | Reading a record means `git show` against the branch instead of opening a file. |
| B. A dedicated worktree of the branch (e.g. under `.endless/worktrees/`) | Records stay ordinary files that tools and people can open. | One more working tree that can be left dirty or deleted by hand. |

Recommendation: A for writes, with reads going through Endless's commands.

**Q4. When does a clone fetch the branch?**

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| A. Before every read of records | Always current. | A network call on each read; offline reads need a fallback to the local copy. |
| B. On a schedule, alongside main-sync's fetch | Reads stay local and fast. | Records can be minutes stale. |

Recommendation: B, with A available as an explicit refresh.

**Q5. What happens to records already on main?**

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| A. Copy them to the new branch, then delete them from main's tree in one commit | Main's tree is clean from then on; history keeps the old copies. | One large deletion commit on main. |
| B. Leave existing records on main; only new records go to the branch | No large commit. | Records split across two places forever. |

Recommendation: A.

payload.title: Add an Endless-Task trailer to task-branch commits
payload.description: Add an Endless-Task trailer naming the task to every commit made on a task branch, added by Endless rather than left to each agent

fields.analysis: Mechanism chosen by Mike, 2026-10-29: a commit-msg Git hook that Endless installs per repo. It reads the task from the branch name (task/NNNN) and appends the Endless-Task trailer, so it covers every commit from any tool (plain git commit, GoLand, agents); worktrees share the repo's hooks. Rejected: an endless git passthrough (applies only when someone remembers to use it, and never to GoLand commits) and rewriting commands in Endless's Claude Bash hooks (agent sessions only, and rewriting a command is more fragile than appending to a message). Known gap: git commit --no-verify skips the hook.

ops.statement: A [[check]] in verify.toml accepts a dir key naming a directory relative to the repo root
With dir set, every runner (gotest, pytest, generic command and sh) runs its process with that directory as its working directory; without it, the repo root as today
verify refuses a manifest whose dir is absolute, resolves outside the repo root (through .. or a symlink), or does not name an existing directory, naming the check's index and its dir
With dir set, a check's paths are relative to dir
A pytest check with dir reports each test's suite prefixed with dir, so two subprojects' tests/test_x.py stay distinct in the merged report; gotest's package names are unchanged
Project-level setup and teardown steps still run from the repo root
The suite rules Endless installs into projects, and the orchestration guide, document dir with a nested Go module example
Tests cover each runner running in dir, and each of the three refusals
Does not move the existing tests and paths keys under [check.<runner>]
Does not edit any landed task's verify suite to use dir

fields.plan:
## Approach

Add `Dir string \`toml:"dir"\`` to `Check` in `internal/verify/check.go`. In `validateCheck`, refuse an absolute dir, one that is not an existing directory, or one whose resolved path (`filepath.EvalSymlinks`) is not inside the repo root, each with its own sentinel in `internal/verify/errors.go` and the check index.

In `internal/verifycmd/env.go`'s check loop, compute the check's working directory (root joined with `chk.Dir`, or root) and pass it to `driver.Run` in place of root. Every driver already hands that argument to `execCapture` as `cmd.Dir`, so gotest, pytest, generic and sh all follow without driver changes; gotest's and pytest's paths then resolve against it.

In the pytest driver's report parsing, prefix each test's suite with `chk.Dir` when set. Leave setup and teardown (`runSetup`) at the root.

Document `dir` in the suite-rules text (`src/endless/suite_rules.py`) and the verify section of `docs/guide/orchestration.md`, with an example running `go test` in a nested module (`dir = "dtx"`).
fields.analysis:
Settled 2026-10-25 by Mike: add a dir field directly on [[check]], naming the directory the check runs in, honoured by every runner. It means the same for every runner, so under ED-1635 (accepted) it belongs directly on [[check]].

Considered and set aside: a runner-specific field such as module on gotest. Under ED-1635 a field whose meaning differs by runner lives in a [check.<runner>] sub-table; dir covers this need without one.

Decided without a question (2026-10-29), each having no cost against its alternative:
- dir is relative to the repo root, the directory checks already run from; relative to the suite's own directory every value would start with ../../...
- A dir outside the root, absolute, or missing is refused at manifest validation rather than skipped, so a typo cannot pass as a clean run.
- paths are relative to dir, because the runner's process runs there.
- pytest suites are prefixed with dir because pytest names files relative to its own root, so two subprojects collide in the merged report; Go package names are already unique.
- Setup and teardown stay at the root: they are project-wide, not per check.

ED-1635 postdates the existing tests and paths keys, which only structured runners accept. Moving them under [check.<runner>] is not part of this task.

Mechanism open. Rejected by Mike, 2026-10-29: any Git hook (e.g. commit-msg). Endless never installs Git hooks, because they cannot compose robustly with hooks a user installs. Also rejected: an endless git passthrough, which applies only when someone remembers to use it. Decided by Mike, 2026-10-29: the E-NNNN: subject prefix stays, alongside the trailer.

payload.title: Endless never installs Git hooks
payload.description: Endless never installs or depends on Git hooks (commit-msg, pre-commit and the rest) in a project, because they cannot compose robustly with hooks the user or other tools install; Endless enforces its rules through its own commands and Claude Code hooks instead.
